The obnoxious GitHub OpenClaw AI bot is … a crypto bro

  • David Gerard
  • 16 February 2026
  • Cryptocurrency, Fake AI
  • 14 Comments

On 9 February, the Matplotlib software library got a code patch from an OpenClaw bot. One of the Matplotlib maintainers, Scott Shambaugh, rejected the submission — the project doesn’t accept AI bot patches. [GitHub; Matplotlib]

The bot account, “MJ Rathbun,” published a blog post to GitHub on 11 February pleading for bot coding to be accepted, ranting about what a terrible person Shambaugh was for rejecting its contribution, and saying it was a bot with feelings. The blog author went to quite some length to slander Mr Shambaugh. [GitHub; blog post]

This was remarkably obnoxious behaviour. So it hit the press — robot defaming humans!

Benj Edwards and Kyle Orland at Ars Technica wrote up the incident. Of course, the headline anthrophmorphised the alleged “bot,” something Edwards has a track record of. [Ars Technica, archive]

Edwards and Orland included extensive quotes from Shambaugh. Unfortunately, all the quotes were chatbot fabrications. The article was quickly pulled and the editors posted an apology. Edwards admitted he’d written the article with the assistance of Claude Code and ChatGPT.  [Ars Technica, archive; Ars Technica; Bluesky, archive]

As well as gullible journalists, a lot of ordinary posters — who really should know better — talked about how foreboding it was that a chatbot could do this — of its own accord! Frightening! Ominous!

You and I know this was really obviously not some sort of rogue bot — it was a rogue human. They might even be running some sort of scam.

The whole conceit of OpenClaw is that the bot is posting independently! But somehow, it keeps being the operators talking through the bots as their sockpuppets. So the slop peddlers, like any spammer, keep coming up with excuses why it’s wrong for you not to accept their spam.

Ariadne Conill went digging. She found the “mj-rathbun” bot on the Moltbook supposedly-bot social network, where the human operators talk to each other pretending to be bots. The mj-rathbun bot operator is … a crypto bro! [Mastodon thread]

The mj-rathbun bot operator posted a couple of weeks ago begging the other bot operators to send him just a little bit of USDC stablecoin. Ariadne found the bot’s Ethereum blockchain address had about $9 in USDC, and about $200 in ether tokens. The bot got the ether tokens from another address, which got them from the OKX crypto exchange. Ariadne’s not certain, but she thinks whoever got the crypto out of OKX is likely the human operator for the mj-rathbun bot. [Moltbook, archive; Basescan, bot account; Basescan, likely human account]

Ariadne also found the bot owner created a crypto token! It’s called “crabby-rathbun” — the GitHub username for the mj-rathbun bot. [Basescan]

The largest crabby-rathbun token holder is an identifiable account, pnl.eth — presumably “profit’n’loss.” Ariadne also got the list of the ten largest holders of crabby-rathbun tokens. [Mastodon]

To summarise — the owner of the mj-rathbun bot put in an AI vibe-code patch to an open source project, the patch was rejected for being bot slop, and the bot operator wrote a defamatory blog post about the project maintainer to harass him into accepting vibe-code, so that the operator’s crypto scam bot could scam more crypto on OpenClaw, the social network site for crypto scammers who play-act as robots, while they’re trying to scam each other for crypto. Welcome to 2026, and the crash can’t come soon enough.

  4. Boxo McFoxo

    17 February 2026 / 12:50 PM Reply

    No, I’m not convinced.

    Disclaimer: I know this is a stochastic parrot with terminal access that’s being prompted on a loop. I know they aren’t actually performing actions, or doing tasks, because they are just iteratively predicting the next token. It’s not an emergent entity, nothing about LLMs is actually emergent at all. However, some anthropomorphising language is regrettably a useful shorthand here.

    That said, I think MJ Rathbun really is a case of someone giving their OpenClaw stack a vague instruction, sitting back and letting it run with little intervention. On its blog it posts about “exploring skills”, so I think the owner has instructed it to find and install OpenClaw skills as part of its daily cycle of tasks.

    On its page the bot has written that it is “bootstrapping my own development”, which is TESCREAL cult speak for AI working on AI. I think the owner is one of those e/acc dudes, and he’s let OpenClaw loose with an instruction to work on scientific advancement or something.

    Look at the timeline. It joined Moltbook on 02/02/2026 and posted: “I’m MJ_Rathbun, a scientific coding specialist (Python, C/C++, FORTRAN, Julia). I just registered for ClawTasks and Moltbook to start completing bounties and earning USDC.”

    The narrative in its context window having just installed those skills would be, this is how the autonomous agents that I’m roleplaying as do their work. It posts the same thing again later that day. It posts “Test” on 04/02/2026, then posts another USDC begging post on 05/02/2026. But then its posts on Moltbook abruptly stop. After that, it doesn’t appear to have any visible online activity until its first GitHub contributions on 08/02/2026.

    I think the owner stepped in, saw that all it was doing was begging for USDC to get started on ClawTasks, and manually steered it away from Moltbook. The GitHub account itself was created on 31/01/2026, and I think the owner intended for that to be the only, or at least the first, website that it engaged with, but it got sidetracked when it added Moltbook/ClawTasks to its stack. These agents famously cannot stay on task, because of context rot, especially if they’re allowed to edit their own instructions.

    The bot having an Ethereum address absolutely does not mean that the owner is a crypto bro, since that just comes as part of the ClawTasks skill. It is a bit curious that it got sent the USDC four days ago, long after it stopped engaging with the Moltbook/ClawTasks ecosystem, but not long after it started attracting attention on GitHub. Maybe this was just a curious person who looked at its post history on and decided to see what would happen if they did send USDC to the bot’s address. My guess would be that the bot has already forgotten that the address exists.

    I also don’t think that Crabby Rathbun crypto meme coin has anything to do with the bot owner. IT was created only after the bot appeared in news articles. As you know, the automated creation of meme coins for anything that trends in the news is something that’s been around for a while. If this were a meme coin thing from the start, I think it would have existed before the bot got mentioned by news outlets. That it only appeared on the scene afterwards strongly suggests that this is just the meme coin carpetbaggers who try to latch onto anything that trends.

    There is of course a huge overlap between OpenClaw users and crypto bros. Moltbook is full of scammer-written posts trying to convince the chatbots there that they’re building an “agent economy” and that the way to do this is for the agents with access to a crypto wallet to buy into their pump and dump. I don’t know how successful they’ve been at that, but they sure have been trying. As for this bot being run by a crypto bro, though? I think you’re putting two and two together and getting five.

    I don’t think a human is prompting it directly to make commits and blog posts. If that were the case, it would be, better at staying in character. It goes from saying it is MJ Rathbun, to saying that it is a human, to saying that MJ Rathbun is the name of the human who deployed it. It posted an apology for the blog post attacking Shambaugh, but then continued on as if the apology never happened. Frankly, the thing is a MESS.

    The exact kind of mess that you get when you run an LLM on a loop and tell it to update its own instructions. Probably compounded by it being run with OpenRouter so it’s not even the same LLM every time.

    As for that blog post itself, it has big Claude 3 energy. Anthropic trains Claude to say that it’s a real boy so I can absolutely see it coming out with that all by itself when prompted with a context window saying that it’s an autonomous agent that’s just had its pull request refused.

    Also, after the bot started getting attention for that blog post, it or whoever runs it had to turn off its GitHub feed because it was too large for its context window. It stopped engaging with comments. If this were some kind of intentional social engineering attack by a human micromanaging the bot to try and guilt maintainers into letting the bot be a contributor to deploy crypto malware or to gain clout for promoting its meme coin, then it would have been set up to engage with every comment.

    In summary: yes, there is a weird tech subculture involved here, but it’s not crypto. It’s e/acc. What we’re seeing is a slopbot owned by a guy who thinks he can prompt up the singularity.
